pr.title: Publish attested, reproducible releases, and check them with install.sh verify
pr.head: 180bd8842df4946d8269fc9ff4cc574adfc52585

summary: multipass is a password manager with no third-party crates, and its installer (the layer below, #27) installs a prebuilt binary only after gh attestation verify proves that the repository's release workflow built it from the tag. That layer assumes releases exist. This layer makes them: a GitHub Actions workflow that publishes each version merged to main, a build script that proves the binary does not depend on where or when it was built, and an install.sh verify command that lets anyone rebuild a release on their own Mac and compare the bytes.

1. Releasing. A merge to main that changes Cargo.toml starts release.yml. Its read-only build job builds the universal binary on a macOS runner. Its publish job, which never checks out the repository, signs a build attestation (a Sigstore-signed statement of which workflow, ref, and commit produced each file) and publishes an immutable release.
  2. Reproducing. .github/scripts/build-release.sh builds each target twice at two paths of different lengths and fails when any byte differs. It writes a build info file that records the toolchain, SDK, and flags.
  3. Checking. install.sh verify <version> downloads the tag's source, the release binary, and the build info, rebuilds this Mac's slice with the named rustup toolchain, and compares it with the release's slice.
The README's install section is unchanged on purpose: the plan adds the release installs to it only at rollout step 7, once the first release and the domain exist.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Build info: multipass-<version>.buildinfo, a release asset of key value lines that says what the build ran on.
  • Slice: one architecture's binary inside the universal file, which lipo joins and splits.
  • -oso_prefix .: a linker flag that records object file paths relative to the build directory, so the binary's UUID does not depend on the path.
  • Bundle: multipass.sigstore.json, the signed attestation, which lets gh attestation verify run without a GitHub login.

groups.title: The release workflow
groups.kicker: Two jobs: a read-only build, and a publish job that runs no repository code
intro: release.yml derives the release from the version in Cargo.toml on main, so a branch or tag name cannot choose what gets published. It runs on a push to main that changes Cargo.toml, and by hand for the first release or after a failed run. Its first step fails on any other ref, because the attestation records the ref the run started from and the installer accepts only refs/heads/main. The build job sets DEVELOPER_DIR to one Xcode on the image, because GitHub moves the image's default Xcode without any change to the workflow, and the SDK version is part of the binary.

The write and signing permissions sit on publish alone, and that job only downloads the artifact, attests two files, and creates the release. It creates the release as a draft with every asset, then publishes it, so nothing is public until all five files are there, and GitHub's immutable releases then lock the tag and assets.

checks.text: Each action is pinned to the commit its tag names in the action's own repository, checked with the GitHub API: actions/checkout v4.4.0, actions/upload-artifact v7.0.2, actions/download-artifact v8.0.2, and actions/attest-build-provenance v4.2.2.
download-artifact v8.0.2 defaults to digest-mismatch: error, read from its action.yml, so publish attests the bytes build uploaded.

files.note: New. The trigger, the per-job permissions, the version check, and the draft-then-publish release.

checks.text: The runner-images README for macos-15 lists /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app as today's default Xcode, so this path exists, and the job's first step fails once the image drops it.
When this lookup fails for any reason, the job goes on to publish, whose gh release create then fails on the existing release. So a transient error cannot replace a published release.

groups.title: The reproducible build
groups.kicker: Build twice at two paths, refuse any difference, record what it took
intro: build-release.sh unpacks git archive HEAD, the same files as GitHub's source archive for the tag, at two directories whose names differ in length. It builds both targets in each with --locked --offline and fails when the bytes differ. Paths of different lengths matter because the linker hashes object file paths into the binary's UUID. The -oso_prefix . flag makes those paths relative, provided the target directory sits inside the unpacked source and the path is the physical one rather than macOS's /var symlink.
The script then joins the two slices with lipo, checks that the result prints its version, and writes SHA256SUMS and the build info.

checks.text: Building this head's source archive at two paths of different lengths with the release flags gave identical aarch64 bytes, tried on a Mac with Rust 1.97.1. The script itself did not run, because that toolchain lacks the x86_64 target.

files.note: New. The double build, the comparison, lipo, and the build info's fields.

groups.title: install.sh verify
groups.kicker: Rebuild a release on your own Mac and compare the bytes
intro: verify replaces trust in GitHub's runner and the attestation with your own build. The build info comes from the build that verify distrusts, so verify accepts only the release build's rustflags and a plain version as the deployment target, and exits 65 naming the field otherwise. It stops with status 69 and the install command when the named rustup toolchain is missing, checks the tag's Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock as a source install does, and builds this Mac's slice. It prints reproduced, or differs with each recorded field that differs on this Mac and exits 65. It installs nothing.

check_release_source now holds the version and lock-file checks for both the source install and verify. make_work resolves the physical path of its temporary directory, so the builds see the path the linker sees. tests/install.sh drives verify against a file:// mirror with a fake rustup.

checks.text: Against a local file:// mirror of this head, with a stand-in rustup over Homebrew's Rust 1.97.1, verify 0.1.0 printed reproduced for an honest build info, and exit 65 for a release built with another deployment target.

files.note: Adds cmd_verify, the verify command, and check_release_source, and makes make_work use the physical path.

checks.text: A mirror whose build info named -C linker=<a script> exited 65 here, and the script never ran.
With a stand-in xcodebuild that exits 1, as on a Mac with only the Command Line Tools, a differing slice printed xcode … this Mac has none, went on to the sdk probe, and exited 65.

files.note: Adds verify cases: a linker in the build info, a deployment target that is not a version, a source that names another version, and a slice that differs where xcodebuild fails.

groups.title: Rules and the plan
groups.kicker: How to cut a release, and the plan brought up to the build as built
intro: AGENTS.md gains a Releases section: release by merging a version bump, never tag by hand, change RUST_VERSION or DEVELOPER_DIR only in a pull request of its own, use only GitHub's actions pinned by full SHA, and keep the build reproducible. The installer plan's § 2.5 and § 2.6 now describe the script, the rustflags field, and verify's exit statuses, and § 8 records why paths of different lengths broke reproducibility. § 2.6 now names the build info's keys as the script writes them and says what verify refuses.

checks.text: The plan stays at status: in-progress and the change adds no open question.
